Subject: Order Form: Availability thresholds & planned outage carveouts

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and engineering reviewed the draft order form and have two main asks before they can sign:

1) Uptime target — they'd like the uptime SLA for the Dedicated tier to be increased to 99.95% (from 99.9%) or, alternatively, to see a change to the service credit multiplier so small outages don't cascade into outsized credits.
2) Planned outages — they want predictable carveouts for planned maintenance windows but also a maximum annual blackout window (they proposed no more than 48 hours total per year for >30s rolling restarts). They also requested an advance notice and an operational point-of-contact during those windows.

I've attached their redline (they called it "Helix_Redline_v1.docx"). Can you confirm Redwood's position on both items? If we can send a single counterproposal with clear fallback language, that would help speed procurement.

Best,
Rina Sethi
Head of Cloud Procurement
HelixCloud

Subject: Re: Order Form: Availability thresholds & planned outage carveouts

Hi Rina — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Looping in Laura (legal) and Aditya (product/ops) to confirm our stance. A few quick thoughts before legal reviews the doc:

- Uptime: Increasing to 99.95% for Dedicated is a material change — we can consider it on a multi-region reserved pool with agreed maintenance windows and a narrower definition of downtime (exclude transient host-level blips). Alternatively we can keep 99.9% but introduce a two-tier credit scale (small, transient events vs sustained outages) so credits are proportional.
- Planned outages: we already offer scheduled maintenance carveouts with 72 hours of planned maintenance per quarter by default in Dedicated; that would exceed Helix's ask for annual caps. However, they want a hard maximum annual blackout of 48 hours — that would constrain our ops flexibility. We should propose an ops SLA that guarantees advance notice (72 hours for non-emergency patches) and an on-call contact for major maintenance, but push back on a strict 48-hour annual ceiling.

Laura/Aditya/Markus — can you review the attached Helix redline and advise on: (a) legal-friendly language we can offer as a compromise for uptime targets, (b) whether the 48-hour annual cap is acceptable or whether we propose alternate language, and (c) whether we should offer a one-time migration credit if they accept 99.9% instead of 99.95%?

I'll compile a single counterproposal once we align.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Availability thresholds & planned outage carveouts

Priyom — quick read and legal perspective:

1) Uptime target: We should avoid unilateral 99.95% for all Dedicated customers. If we consider 99.95% it must be scoped to specific regions/instance classes and tied to a revenue/commitment band. Legally, we can offer an optional Availability Addendum template that customers can check and attach to the order form for an additional fee. This addendum must specify measurement windows, excluded events, and the credit calculation (cap credits at monthly invoice or X%—we typically cap at 50% of monthly fees).

2) Credits: Recommend a tiered credit schedule with thresholds (e.g., <2 hours/month = 0 credits; 2-60 minutes = small credit; >60 minutes = larger credit) — this avoids outsized credits for transient issues. Keep an overall annual cap.

3) Planned outages: We should not agree to a strict 48-hour annual blackout. Suggest alternative language: "Planned maintenance windows will be scheduled with at least 72 hours' notice; Redwood will provide an annual maintenance calendar summary and a named operational contact for critical windows. Unplanned emergency maintenance will be limited to activities required to prevent material service degradation and will be communicated ASAP."

4) Operational POC: Fine to provide an ops contact and an SLA for notification windows, but any on-call responsibilities should be limited to communication and incident coordination; we should not allow customers to dictate operational runbooks.

If Sales wants to be competitive, we can offer the Availability Addendum + a one-time service credit/migration discount. Otherwise, push back to 99.9% with the tiered credit model.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: Availability thresholds & planned outage carveouts

Quick ops input from my side:

- Measurement: We measure uptime at the route-level per calendar month using our standard monitoring pipelines. For Dedicated: if Helix wants 99.95% we must restrict to steady-state traffic patterns with pinned instance pools and specify the measurement method (rolling 30-day window vs calendar month). 99.95% for short-sequence gen workloads with bursty traffic is risky.
- Maintenance: 48 hours/year hard cap is operationally restrictive. We can agree to an annual "maintenance budget" expressed as hours but must allow burst scheduling (e.g., multiple 1-2 hour windows) rather than a single block. We also need to preserve our right to emergency maintenance.
- Credit mechanics: propose a formula: credit = min((downtime_minutes / minutes_in_month) * monthly_fee, cap_percentage * monthly_fee), with thresholds to avoid payouts for micro blips (<30s).

I'm attaching a short internal doc on uptime measurement and a sample Addendum language (I'll send the doc separately to Laura). If Sales wants to sweeten the deal: offer a first-year waiver for one maintenance blackout <= 8 hours if they take a 12-month commit.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Director, Product Ops | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form: Availability thresholds & planned outage carveouts

Hi Rina — thank you for the patience while we reviewed Helix's redline. Attached is our proposed counter-redline (Redwood_OrderForm_redline_v3.docx) and a short PDF that explains how we calculate uptime and credits. High-level summary:

- Uptime: We are prepared to offer an optional Availability Addendum that allows a scoped 99.95% target for Dedicated pools if Helix commits to a 12-month reserved capacity band and accepts the measurement method in the addendum (rolling 30-day measurement, pinned region/instance class). If Helix does not want the Addendum, our default remains 99.9% with the tiered credit schedule included in the counter-redline.
- Credits: We've proposed a tiered credit schedule with thresholds to protect against micro blips and an annual cap (see doc).
- Planned maintenance: We cannot agree to a hard 48-hour annual maximum. Instead we propose a "maintenance budget" expressed as aggregated hours per year with a scheduling mechanism (advance notice of 72 hours, an annual calendar, and one named ops contact). For customers that need stricter windows, we can negotiate a paid maintenance SLA option.

Next steps: If Helix wants the 99.95% Addendum we will route to finance/legal for the pricing amendment. Otherwise please review the attached counter-redline and let me know any specific line items you want us to rework.

Thanks and looking forward to closing this out soon.

Best,
